title: Make an experiment distinguish competing explanations
rule: State an observation, hypothesis, measurable prediction, and controlled comparison. A successful run is not proof of the hypothesis; compare against the recorded baseline and treat small differences as uncertain.
applicability: Project evaluation discipline; all model families.
source: Project protocol: measured task scores, matched starting models and budgets.

title: Warmup, stable learning rate, then decay
rule: A cooldown may reveal progress masked by high-learning-rate fluctuations. Test against a matched continuation; peak LR and cooldown duration still require validation.
applicability: Published theory assumes river-valley structure and experiments concern language-model pretraining. MLP use is an exploratory transfer, not an established advantage. This v1 implements linear warmup and linear terminal decay, not WSD-S checkpoint reuse.

title: Conventional hyperparameter optimization
rule: Bayesian search and resource allocation are strong alternatives for numeric tuning. Agent experiments should justify their extra cost.
applicability: Reference method. The built-in v1 baseline is explicitly random search; BOHB is not implemented or claimed.

title: Hyperparameter transfer across width
rule: A compatible smaller model under maximal-update parameterization can inform settings for a wider model.
applicability: Requires correct parameterization and supported architecture changes. Not implemented by the standard-parameterized MLP adapter.

title: Inspect activation, weight, and update magnitudes
rule: Measure magnitude drift before selecting an intervention. Use an unchanged external evaluation objective if changing loss weights or noise sampling.
applicability: Future diffusion adapter; no diffusion training is implemented in v1.
